narrative_passages.title: The town and the man who came running

summary_for_children: Ya-Sin is called the heart of the Quran. It tells of a town that rejected messengers and a man who came running to support them. It shows signs: dead earth made alive, the night, the sun and moon, and ships at sea.
environment_concept: Dead earth that bursts with grain (36:33), palms and springs (36:34), the moon's phases (36:39), a laden ship (36:41) and a green tree with a fire (36:80).
architecture_and_scenery: A town with a messenger's road, palm and vine gardens, springs, a shoreline with a laden ship, and a huge night sky.

palette.lighting: Dusk to night to dawn cycle; moon phases

unique_world.visual_theme: A quiet hilltop at night with a calendar board of seven hooks, a rack of painted moon discs, palms and olive trees, and a large moon in the sky

primary_mechanic.text: Each night look up at the moon, choose the painted disc with the same shape (thin or round, lit on the right or the left) and hang it on that night's hook. The nights pass and the sky moon changes, from a thin new crescent to full and back to a thin old crescent like an old date stalk (36:39). A disc that does not match goes back with a hint.

secondary_activities: the dead earth brought to life (36:33-35)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The sign of the earth, seven nights at the calendar, then the reading on night and the sun
world_assets: rack of seven painted moon discs
large phase-changing moon in the night sky
environment_behaviour: the sky moon changes phase after each correct night
hung discs stay on the board
unique_world.learning_objective: Watch the moon's stages (36:39-40) and learn that each thing in the sky keeps its own orbit

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The People of the Town
story_library.children_narration: The Quran tells us about a town to which messengers were sent. When the people rejected them, a man came from the farthest part of the city and urged his people to follow the messengers. He showed courage by standing for what he believed was true. The surah then invites us to reflect on the earth, plants, night, day, and the movement of heavenly bodies.

world_idea.title: The Town and the Turning Sky
world_idea.description: Investigate the town narrative through environmental clues, then explore an interactive astronomy observatory.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The man from the far end of the city (36:20-27) is not shown. His killing is not mentioned in the Quran and is not added.
